title: Excavations in Palestine in 1931-2: Tall en Nasba
author: (round-up; expedition directed by W. F. Badé)
screen_term: Tall en Nasba (Tell en-Nasbeh; not in the gazetteer)
location_note: Tell en-Nasbeh north of Jerusalem near the Jerusalem-Nablus road; no map reference. INFERENCE: placed in Z4 by its known position (about 31.885 N, 35.217 E, inside the Z4 box); no distance computed.
notes: 1931 season: Iron Age city wall and east gate (c. 900-700 BC), houses over the wall, destruction level of the Maccabean period (coin of Alexander Balas), Astarte sanctuary enclosure; west necropolis tombs; Jaazaniah seal from the central pit of a re-used Iron Age tomb.

features.subtype: Iron Age tombs (one with central pit) and at least three wholly Bronze Age tombs; largest tomb with Early Bronze to Early Iron deposits
features.period: Bronze Age and Iron Age (original cutting and use)
features.quote: three tombs were found which belong entirely to the Bronze Age

features.subtype: Iron Age tombs re-used and enlarged in the Roman and Byzantine periods; a late Roman and Byzantine tomb with an inscribed lamp
features.quote: re-used and enlarged during the Roman and Byzantine periods
